Choose occupations that interact and communicate directly with the physical world, or occupations that provide emotional value to people. After taking a look, I also became deeply worried. The first category is high-tech chip production and manufacturing jobs. These are relatively comfortable and well paid, and they require strong technical skills. But only a small number of people can get in. The second category involves AI equipment and all the related equipment it creates: installation, repair, and maintenance jobs, such as electricians, plumbers, and data-center maintenance technicians. The barriers to entry are relatively high, and they require years of training. Their wages will rise substantially. The third category is healthcare and nursing, including caregivers, care for elderly clients, and jobs in the beauty industry. In short, these are mainly blue-collar jobs. The highest-paid workers will be licensed master electricians, plumbers, and installers. But obtaining these licenses generally takes five or even ten years of experience. The work is very dangerous. It is either exhausting, or it means working outdoors in all weather. You don't have to worry about the income. In places like Europe and North America, blue-collar plumbers and electricians are extremely scarce and highly desirable. One part sweat brings ten parts reward. If you don't want to work for someone else and want to make money in the AI era, one remaining option is to become your own boss, discover a way to combine AI and human labor, find a profitable secret, and quietly make a fortune. Finally, only one most important path remains, and we can start preparing for it now: investing. Anthropic's report says that returns on capital will explode in the AI era. There are three underlying reasons. The first is computing power, which carries a scarcity premium relative to capital. By 2030, data centers, chips, and computing capacity will not be able to expand infinitely overnight. They will therefore face various shortages. The scarcer they are, the more the AI computing chain can extract excess rents and returns at every stage. That includes chips, electricity, and packaging, as well as the various other upstream and downstream links. This can drive net returns on capital sharply higher. In other words, the upstream and downstream AI buildout is scarce, so we can earn excess profits from it. Second, AI automation will transform what was once the white-collar wage bill into returns on capital through AI agents. Their core function is complete automation. Companies no longer need people to do the work; data centers can do it instead. The report says that by 2030, capital's share of GDP could rise from the previous 40% to 43.9%, and in the extreme scenario, capital could generate 54.8% of GDP. This means that if, in the future, a country earns one trillion U.S. dollars, 540 billion dollars of that amount will be generated by capital invested in AI. So by that time, labor may be honorable, but labor will no longer be valuable. AI data centers will make all the money. The third core reason is that AI will cause overall global productivity to surge. GDP will soar. U.S. GDP could reach 15%, or even 30%. Without AI, returns on capital might only match the S&P 500 average, around 6%. But with AI, the average return on capital could rise to 8%–10%. That is only the average. For leading AI companies, returns on stocks like these could be several times higher. Hold on to your chip stocks, memory stocks, CPU, GPU, and optical-interconnect stocks, and finally, data centers. These are the investment themes of this era.
